blocks.x: I have been requested by Haywood Haley to give you some history on the New Orleans Jazz of the city of New Orleans. This is Jack Kerrigan speaking. I was born March of 18, 1900, and my first contact with jazz was when I lived in Hammond around 19... 17 at the old Oaks Hotel. Saturday night dances used to be given quite often and my first opportunity to hear the New Orleans Jazz was given... was played by a band from Baton Rouge known as Johnson's Band. Later on after finishing my high school in Hammond I moved to New Orleans and entered Tulane year 1918. and at that time jazz was beginning and becoming the most popular type of music to be enjoyed by the Tulane students. and in fact the gym dances given at the old gym was a very very popular spot and only jazz was wanted by the students. Later on I became a member of the Southern Yacht Club and every dance there we always had jazz music. Of course the dances stopped at 12 o'clock in those days and there was a very lively spot located at the Spanish port known as... um... Tranchinas. To me this was the hottest spot in town due to the fact that they had the old P-ROM band playing there every Sunday... every Saturday... on into Sunday morning. This band in my opinion in later years became the outstanding jazz band in the city of New Orleans. In addition to playing there on Saturday night as this type of music became very very popular... P-ROMs was the band used by the New Orleans Country Club for their Saturday afternoon and Sunday afternoon... Tate-en-sons. As this music became very popular the old Louisiana restaurant... had dances on Wednesday evening and Saturday evening... and at this place... the band used was known as Robichaux. All colored band... the leader was a left-handed violin player known as Robichaux. That's where the band got its name. Numerous times... we all gathered at the Louisiana when... especially on Wednesday night... or when there was a private party at the country club... which prevented us from going there... we went to hear Robichaux play. Another spot that we had the... opportunity of hearing outstanding jazz music... was at the halfway house... which had... a very very popular... Dixieland jazz band. Another spot... was... at... Cobb's restaurant... and at... that spot... Johnny Detroit... started his... jazz band. I recall that... from... the early twenties... on into... the... let's say as far as 1926-27. All debutante parties... the country club... the St. Charles Hotel... and the Gold Room... were spots... used to... give the... debutante parties. Also the Roosevelt Hotel... and private homes... requested... or used... jazz bands... approximately... 98% of the parties given. I'm now living on the coast... at Paz Christiane... and... whenever they want to put up... dance over... at the art club here... jazz is called upon... and... at the present time... we are still... using... Celestine's band... which was... one of the outstanding... colored bands... in the later years of jazz... in the city of New Orleans... well... do you...

remember... if at any time... they... stopped... using it... at... at... at... at parties... and then... when... it started again... when... if people... stopped liking it... and stopped listening to it... then started again... you know... like... the death of jazz... and the revival... in the... early 40's... and so on... do you... remember anything? moved away from...
